prompt: A solid alloy has a density of $2.5\text{ g cm}^{-3}$. What is this density expressed in SI base units ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$)?
distractor_explanations: Incorrect. Divided by 1000 instead of multiplying by 1000; forgot that cm^3 is in the denominator.
Incorrect. Only replaced cm with 10^-2 m without cubing to 10^-6 m^3.
Incorrect. Inverted the factor between g and kg.
hints: Convert grams to kilograms: 1 g = 10^-3 kg.
Divide the mass factor by the volume factor: 10^-3 / 10^-6.
teacher_walkthrough: Classic Cambridge prefix and derived unit conversion trap.
Show why water at 1.0 g/cm^3 has density 1000 kg/m^3.

provenance.abstract_pattern: compound unit conversion with cubed prefix
provenance.independence_statement: Authored as an original item converting density from CGS to SI base units.
